doc.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
doc.interviewee: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack")

title: Mary Mack's Merry Makers: the company name and a 1926 handbill
summary: Allen passes on Professor Minetta's regards and asks about the name Mary Mack. The company began as the Southern Comedy Company and was renamed for Mary; a 1926 program from Prince's Theatre, Youngstown, is identified.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Yes. 28th of July. Before I forget it, I don't think I'll forget it, but Professor Minetta has mentioned Mary Mack. I didn't know if you were known by that name. Mary Mack, yes. At that time. He mentioned that Mary Mack came from Algiers and was a wonderful singer and entertainer. I know he would send his regards. He didn't know I was going to see you. Well, I'd be glad. And I see him almost every Tuesday night. I go over to his studio where he teaches and I record a little interview with him. I see. And when he teaches some of his lessons, talking about music, too. Yes. He's still active. Oh, I'm so glad to hear that. So he'll be glad to hear your voice. If you don't mind, I'll play him this tape sometime. I think he would enjoy
hearing your voice again. Well, I would be glad for you to play, for him to hear. Me and Mac. Yes, and we had, we were known in show business as Mary Mack's Merry Makers. Oh, yes.

Uh-huh. That record that you made with Kid Punch is called that, I remember. The Merry Makers Twine? Well, oh, that, no, that was a Lovie Austin record, wasn't it? No, Lovie Austin played it, but that's our record. I know. I mean, she made a record of it once. Yes. Oh, yes, she did. That's

quite a while back. Now, what did that mean, that Merry Makers Twine? Well, you can see here, this is the name of the company. We call it at first, the Southern Comedy Company, but after we got a little better organized and more people added to the show, we named it after the wife, Mary. Oh, yes.

Mac's Merry Makers. Mary Mac's Merry Makers Company. Oh, yes. And Billy Mac presents that twirly-girly jazz comedy Jubilee. That's it? Yeah. This was the little program that... That we had, yes. You had. This was back in 19... No? 26. 1926. At that, yes. In November. Yes. Which city was this in? I think that was in Youngstown, Ohio.
Federal Street, yes. I don't recognize. Yeah, Federal Street. That's the Prince's Theatre. Oh, yes. Here it tells on the front.
